A Study on Industrial Safety Design of SMEs Smart Factory According to the Digital Transformation of the Industry - Focus on the ʹTʹ company in the Smart Green Industrial Complex -

Lee, Youngju First Author. Doctor of Fine Arts, Spatial Design, Hongik University Graduate School

(Background and Purpose) The digital transformation of the industry is affecting the consumer market, transforming it into a consumer-centered market with mass customization. Accordingly, small and medium-sized enterprises(SMEs) are introducing smart factories that apply smart production systems to produce goods tailored to consumer demand. Workers in smart factories are required to have new job competencies and work methods, such as monitoring smart facilities and collaborating with robots, and collaborative tasks with new machines, such as collaborative robots and autonomous mobile logistics robots, has the potential to cause another type of industrial accident, which requires preparation. In particular, it focused on the need for an order system in terms of design to minimize workers' cognitive behavior errors, paying attention to the fact that a very high proportion of industrial accidents in the manufacturing industry are caused by work blunders.
Therefore, the purpose of this study is to provide fundamental data for the planning and design stage of the industrial environment by conducting an empirical analysis that focuses on the most successful instances of industrial safety design applied to smart factories for SMEs. (Method) Based on prior research into spatial functions and roles within smart factory manufacturing processes for SMEs, this study analyzed the guidelines and manuals relating to industrial safety design in Korea. From this analysis, it identified specific design application items and components and used these to derive research findings on the direction of the industrial safety design approach in SMEs smart factory by building a case analysis model and selecting and analyzing the best cases of industrial safety design application. (Results) Upon the analysis, findings showed that ʹTʹ company enhanced the work environment by utilising multiple components for each industrial safety design component to avert safety hazards. Furthermore, previous studies have identified that two aspects of industrial safety design, ʹSignageʹ and ʹFacilities and Equipmentʹ, are effective as the scope of industrial safety design application for SMEs smart factory. It has been determined that the set of five components, ʹNCL Block Designationʹ, ʹDesignated Fontʹ,  ʹ Pictogramʹ, ʹSafety Facilityʹ,and ʹFirefighting and Electricityʹ, derived for each application item and 13 detailed components are all suitable as industrial safety design components. (Conclusions) Through the study, it was found that an order system in terms of design for hazards is needed based on material, human, and management factors centered on workers in order to ensure worker safety in smart factories for SMEs. It has been confirmed that the application of industrial safety design in smart factories for SMEs is important to approach from a preventive perspective rather than a reactive response to change workers' safety cognitive behavior, thereby contributing to work stress reduction and work efficiency.

A Study on Industrial Safety Design of SMEs Smart Factory According to the Digital Transformation of the Industry - Focus on the ʹTʹ company in the Smart Green Industrial Complex -

Lee, Youngju First Author. Doctor of Fine Arts, Spatial Design, Hongik University Graduate School

(Background and Purpose) The digital transformation of the industry is affecting the consumer market, transforming it into a consumer-centered market with mass customization. Accordingly, small and medium-sized enterprises(SMEs) are introducing smart factories that apply smart production systems to produce goods tailored to consumer demand. Workers in smart factories are required to have new job competencies and work methods, such as monitoring smart facilities and collaborating with robots, and collaborative tasks with new machines, such as collaborative robots and autonomous mobile logistics robots, has the potential to cause another type of industrial accident, which requires preparation. In particular, it focused on the need for an order system in terms of design to minimize workers' cognitive behavior errors, paying attention to the fact that a very high proportion of industrial accidents in the manufacturing industry are caused by work blunders.
Therefore, the purpose of this study is to provide fundamental data for the planning and design stage of the industrial environment by conducting an empirical analysis that focuses on the most successful instances of industrial safety design applied to smart factories for SMEs. (Method) Based on prior research into spatial functions and roles within smart factory manufacturing processes for SMEs, this study analyzed the guidelines and manuals relating to industrial safety design in Korea. From this analysis, it identified specific design application items and components and used these to derive research findings on the direction of the industrial safety design approach in SMEs smart factory by building a case analysis model and selecting and analyzing the best cases of industrial safety design application. (Results) Upon the analysis, findings showed that ʹTʹ company enhanced the work environment by utilising multiple components for each industrial safety design component to avert safety hazards. Furthermore, previous studies have identified that two aspects of industrial safety design, ʹSignageʹ and ʹFacilities and Equipmentʹ, are effective as the scope of industrial safety design application for SMEs smart factory. It has been determined that the set of five components, ʹNCL Block Designationʹ, ʹDesignated Fontʹ,  ʹ Pictogramʹ, ʹSafety Facilityʹ,and ʹFirefighting and Electricityʹ, derived for each application item and 13 detailed components are all suitable as industrial safety design components. (Conclusions) Through the study, it was found that an order system in terms of design for hazards is needed based on material, human, and management factors centered on workers in order to ensure worker safety in smart factories for SMEs. It has been confirmed that the application of industrial safety design in smart factories for SMEs is important to approach from a preventive perspective rather than a reactive response to change workers' safety cognitive behavior, thereby contributing to work stress reduction and work efficiency.

sections.title: 다. 따라서 선행연구를 통해 추출한 항목 중 지속유지
sections.content:
디자인 개념과 범위를 체계화하고 기본방향을 제시하 관리를 위한 ʹ교육ᆞ관리시스템ʹ과 작업자를 적용대상 였다. 이후 서울시에서는 ʹ2022년 서울안전디자인 매 으로 한 ʹ개인보호구ʹ 등을 제외한 범위에서 산업안전 뉴얼ʹ을 수립하여 산업안전디자인 적용지침을 제시하 디자인 적용 항목 및 구성요소를 추출하였다.
고 있다.
추출된 산업안전디자인 항목은 크게 두 가지로 구 이와 함께 산업전반의 디지털 전환과 맞물려 중소 분해볼 수 있다. 첫 번째는 작업장 내 환경정보 시각 제조기업 스마트팩토리 보급이 확산되면서, 스마트제 매체로서의 범위를 가지는 사이니지로서,  NCL 블록 조혁신추진단은 변화하는 근로환경의 산업재해를 줄이 지정, 지정서체, 픽토그램을 포함하며, 두 번째는 시설 기 위해 2022년 ʹ스마트공장 작업환경개선모델 적용 및 설비를 포함하는 전반적인 요소로서 안전시설, 소 가이드ʹ를 수립하여 스마트팩토리 내 안전한 작업환경 방시설 및 전기설비로 나눠볼 수 있다.
조성을 위해 디자인적 측면에서 노력하고 있다.

및 시설로서 제어자동화 시설의 작업현황 파악을 위한   으로 이를 기준으로 산업안전디자인을 적용한 제조기

ʹAI기반 실시간 모니터링 플랫폼ʹ은 생산 공정별로 구  업 사례가 확대될 것으로 예측되므로, 이들 사례들을

분하여 코드화된 정위치를 지정하여 배치.관리하는 것   대상으로 하는 연구 또한 필요할 것으로 보여진다. 또

이 필요하다. 이와 함께 자동화 기계설비는 작업자가  한 본 연구에서는 산업사고 재해율이 가장 높은 ʹ기계

인접하여 발생할 수 있는 안전사고를 미연에 방지하기   기구ᆞ금속ᆞ비금속광물 제품제조업ʹ을 중심으로 연구

위해 시각적으로 눈에 잘 띌 수 있는 색상을 적용하는   하였으나, 이외 세부업종에서도 산업재해 발생이 지속

것이 필요하며, 이를 위해 주변 배경색과 구분되는 기   되고 있는 점을 감안하면 업종별로 연구가 진행되어야

조색을 공통으로 적용하는 것이 필요함을 알 수 있었  할 것으로 예상된다.

다. 또한 협업용ᆞ산업용 로봇의 경우 작업자와의 안    그러므로 본 연구는 중소제조기업 중 ʹ기계기구ᆞ금

전거리 유지 및 이를 위한 작업공간 확보가 중요하므   속ᆞ비금속광물 제품제조업ʹ을 중심으로 스마트팩토리

로 안전색을 적용한 경계구역 지정은 필수이다. 자율   도입 시 고려해야할 산업안전디자인에 대한 기획 및

주행 방식의 이동형 로봇은 작업자와 부딪침 방지를   디자인 단계에서의 방향성을 제시하는 기초자료로 활

위해 동선을 구분하되, 명확한 주정차 위치를 작업자   용되는 것에 의의를 두며, 후속 연구에서는 업종별 다

가 사전에 인지할 수 있도록 하여 공간적 질서를 부여   수사례를 중심으로 확대 진행하고자 한다.
